findings.description: ACTUAL_COUNT now counts Git index entries rather than files present on disk. git ls-files continues listing tracked files after they have been deleted from the working tree.
findings.failure_mode: Deleting a tracked .claude script or configuration file without staging the deletion leaves ACTUAL_COUNT unchanged. Preflight therefore stops reporting the file-count mismatch for an incomplete installation, allowing missing runtime components to pass this integrity check.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Git to select the manifest's scope, then count only selected paths that exist in MANIFEST_TREE. Preserve the upstream-tree handling for submodule mounts.

findings.description: In a submodule mount (.loa/.claude is a directory) any manifest path that is absent from .claude/ but present under .loa/ is now counted as informational 'not-mounted' instead of 'Missing'. The check has no notion of which paths the mount actually linked, so a linked file that is later deleted (e.g. a hook or gate script symlink removed via a Bash command, which implement-gate does not fence) is indistinguishable from a path the mount never linked. Before this change that deletion produced `fail "Missing: ..."`; now the run prints a count and 'Integrity verified'. The SDD intent (don't fail on designed-unlinked paths) does not require ignoring removal of previously linked paths.
findings.failure_mode: System Zone self-check reports 'Integrity verified' after a fence script or rule file is deleted from a submodule-mounted .claude/, defeating the tamper detection the check exists for.
findings.suggested_fix: Only classify a path as not-mounted when it is absent from the mount's link list (the set of .claude/ entries recorded at mount time by sandbox-mount.sh / the mount manifest); otherwise keep `fail "Missing: $file"`. At minimum print each not-mounted path (not just a count) so a removed link is visible, and compare the count against the expected unlinked set.

findings.description: The new unconditional `return 0` means check_integrity no longer propagates drift through its return status. Previously the trailing `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...` returned 1 on tamper/missing, which under `set -e` aborted the script with a non-zero exit. Whether tampering still affects the process exit code now depends entirely on `fail` incrementing a global counter that the main flow checks.
findings.failure_mode: If `fail` only prints, a tampered/missing System Zone file yields exit 0 from check-loa.sh and callers (CI, preflight) treat the tree as clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `fail` sets a failure counter consulted at exit, or `return 1` when drift=true and have the caller handle it explicitly (`check_integrity || DRIFT=1`) rather than masking the status.

findings.cross_file_justification: codex-headless now hops to gpt-6.1-sol for pricing (test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py asserts the hop), so every codex MODELINV/ledger row and the ablation cost ledgers (spend.sh cap watchdog, ablation-row.sh cost_usd/voice_cost_usd) are priced from a placeholder copied from gpt-5.5.
findings.description: gpt-6.1-sol's rate card is explicitly a PLACEHOLDER (gpt-5.5 list prices) yet the ledger will record these rows with `pricing_source: config` and `pricing_resolution: hop/exact`, indistinguishable from confirmed pricing. Nothing in the catalog or ledger marks the estimate as unconfirmed.
findings.failure_mode: Spend caps, MODELINV cost totals and ablation runs.jsonl cost_usd are silently wrong for every codex hop until the rate card is confirmed; if gpt-6.1 is priced higher, batch caps under-trigger.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a machine-readable marker (e.g. `pricing.confirmed: false` / `pricing.placeholder_of: gpt-5.5`) that find_pricing surfaces as `cost_estimated: true` or a distinct `pricing_source`, and have the bead that confirms the rate card remove it. Alternatively point the hop at an entry with confirmed pricing and document the mismatch.

findings.description: Every input (pipeline.json, both dissent envelopes, the full MODELINV ledger wrapped with line numbers, task yaml, manifest, dot-writes) is passed to jq via `--argjson` on the command line. Linux caps a single argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128 KiB). Dissent envelopes with many findings or a MODELINV ledger from a full review+audit run can exceed this.
findings.failure_mode: `jq: Argument list too long` (E2BIG); under `set -e` the script exits non-zero and no row is appended to runs.jsonl for that run, so the batch silently loses rows for exactly the largest (most interesting) runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the large inputs to temp files and load them with `--slurpfile`/`--rawfile` (or feed them on stdin as one combined object), keeping only small scalars as `--arg`.

findings.description: `ms(ts)` strips only a fractional-seconds `.NNNZ` suffix before `fromdateiso8601`, which accepts only `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`. Any `started`/`finished` value with a numeric offset (`+00:00`), a space separator, an empty string (the row emits `started // ""`) or a numeric epoch raises a jq runtime error. Several other fields (`$g.recall.*`, `e.metadata.companion_voice`, `.payload.effort_effective`) likewise index into values whose type is not checked.
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed timestamp or an unexpected grade/envelope shape makes the whole jq program fail and the run produces no row (exit non-zero), rather than a row with that field null.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard with `try ... catch null` (e.g. `try (ts | ... | fromdateiso8601 * 1000) catch null`) and type checks (`if type == "object"`) so one bad field degrades to null instead of aborting the row.

findings.description: Tool versions are captured with `2>&1` and only the first line is kept, so any stderr noise emitted before the version line (update nags, deprecation or NODE_OPTIONS warnings, missing-daemon notices) becomes the recorded `tool=` value and changes the fingerprint between otherwise identical runs. Separately, line 54 hard-codes a per-operator path (`$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats`) as the bats fallback.
findings.failure_mode: Non-reproducible `fp:` values (and therefore `image_digest` in host mode) across runs in the same batch; a batch comparison tool treats identical toolchains as different.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture stdout only (`2>/dev/null`), optionally falling back to stderr if stdout is empty; drop the personal dotfiles path in favour of `LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN`/PATH lookup only.
